summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for an acute flare of chronic pancreatitis, presenting with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and persistent vomiting. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and her standard IV pain and anti-nausea regimen, including Dilaudid, Ketorolac, Phenergan, and Ondansetron. Her pain gradually improved, and she was advanced from NPO to clear liquids, then to a regular diet. She restarted her home oral medications, including methadone, amitriptyline, and lisinopril, with a temporary increase in lisinopril dose for blood pressure control. Due to subtherapeutic INR on admission, she was bridged with daily Lovenox while restarting Coumadin, with discharge instructions to take 10 mg Coumadin on the evening of discharge, then 7.5 mg daily, continuing Lovenox until INR was therapeutic for over 24 hours. Her J-tube and port site remained clean, and she remained ambulatory throughout. She was discharged home with home health support for anticoagulation management and follow-up arranged.
